To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NOX2 is activated in ND and that gut permeability is increased in ND, and that this is associated with oxidative stress.
1) ND patients have higher NOX2 activation than CT; 2) NOX2 activation is associated with gut permeability; 3) NOX2 is associated with oxidative stress; 4) NOX2 activity is associated with LPS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of oxidative stress in the pathogenesis of ND.
the role of oxidative stress and gut-derived LPS in ND.
the study of the role of NOX2 in neurodegenerative diseases and the possible role of gut microbiota in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NOX2 activation is a potential therapeutic target for ND.
NOX2 is involved in the pathogenesis of ND.
NOX2 activation, oxidative stress and increased gut permeability may play a role in the physiopathology of ND.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the gut microbiota, by increasing the gut permeability, could lead to the translocation of bacterial products (LPS) in the systemic circulation, which could in turn increase the oxidative stress and inflammation, and finally lead to ND.
the gut microbiome is a key factor in the pathogenesis of ND and that NOX2 activation could be a target in the treatment of ND.
the gut microbiota, through the production of LPS and NOX2 activation, could be implicated in the pathogenesis of ND.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut microbiome may play a role in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases.
gut permeability is a major factor that could explain the increased oxidative stress in ND, and therefore, gut permeability may be a potential therapeutic target for these diseases.
the gut microbiota, in particular Gram negative bacteria, could be a source of LPS and oxidative stress that could be involved in the neuroinflammatory process.
